name: diamond
description: The hardest natural material. Light carbon atoms and stiff bonds give some of the highest-pitched vibrations here.

name: silicon
description: The material of computer chips. The same structure as diamond with heavier atoms, so the whole spectrum drops.

name: gallium arsenide
description: Diamond's structure with two atoms of almost the same mass. In lasers, LEDs and the solar panels of satellites.

name: gallium phosphide
description: Used in early red and green LEDs. Lighter phosphorus lifts the top of the spectrum compared with GaAs.

name: gallium nitride
description: The material behind blue LEDs (Nobel Prize 2014) and small, fast phone chargers.

name: indium phosphide
description: Sends and receives the light signals in fibre-optic networks.

name: aluminium nitride
description: A ceramic that carries heat well but not electricity, used to cool electronics.

name: aluminium phosphide
description: Releases phosphine gas when wet, so it is used to fumigate stored grain.

name: aluminium arsenide
description: Almost exactly the size of GaAs, so layers of the two grow neatly together in laser diodes.

name: cubic boron nitride
description: Diamond's structure built from boron and nitrogen. Nearly as hard as diamond and used in cutting tools.

name: boron arsenide
description: Light boron and heavy arsenic leave a big gap between low and high peaks. It conducts heat almost as well as diamond.

name: boron phosphide
description: A hard, chemically tough semiconductor. Light atoms and stiff bonds put it high in pitch.

name: zinc oxide
description: The white in sunscreen and nappy cream. It also turns squeezing into voltage (piezoelectric).

name: zinc blende
description: The mineral sphalerite, the main ore of zinc. It gave its name to the crystal structure of GaAs and its relatives.

name: zinc selenide
description: Clear to infrared light. Used for the lenses and windows of carbon dioxide lasers.

name: zinc telluride
description: Used to make and detect terahertz pulses, the same frequency range as the vibrations you are hearing.

name: cadmium sulfide
description: The pigment cadmium yellow. Also used in light-dependent resistors.

name: cadmium selenide
description: Tiny crystals of it are the quantum dots that glow in some TV screens.

name: cadmium telluride
description: Thin-film solar panels. Heavy atoms, low frequencies.

name: beryllium oxide
description: Very light atoms. An electrical insulator that conducts heat better than many metals.

name: silicon carbide (3C)
description: The gem moissanite. Hard, and found in the power electronics of electric cars.

name: silicon carbide (4H)
description: The same atoms as 3C silicon carbide, stacked differently. The form used in most power chips.

name: copper iodide
description: A rare see-through semiconductor that conducts positive charges.

name: rock salt
description: Table salt. Familiar, simple and soft.

name: potassium chloride
description: Low-sodium salt. The same structure as rock salt, with heavier potassium in place of sodium.

name: lithium fluoride
description: The lightest salt, made of lithium and fluorine. Its crystals let through ultraviolet light.

name: sodium fluoride
description: The fluoride in toothpaste.

name: potassium bromide
description: Pressed into clear discs to hold samples for infrared spectroscopy. Once a sedative.

name: potassium iodide
description: Taken to protect the thyroid after a nuclear accident.

name: lithium chloride
description: Pulls water out of the air so strongly that it is used in dehumidifiers.

name: caesium chloride
description: Gave its name to a simple cubic structure where each atom has eight neighbours, not rock salt's six.

name: silver chloride
description: Darkens in light. Used in early photography and in reference electrodes.

name: silver bromide
description: The light-sensitive grains in black-and-white photographic film.

name: strontium fluoride
description: Fluorite's structure with heavier strontium, a step down in pitch from calcium fluoride.

name: barium fluoride
description: One of the fastest scintillators, flashing ultraviolet light when hit by radiation.

name: magnesium fluoride
description: The anti-reflection coating on many camera lenses.

name: magnesium oxide
description: Rock salt's structure with stiffer bonds, so it sounds higher. Lines furnaces.

name: calcium oxide
description: Quicklime, made by heating limestone. Heated in a flame it glows white, the original "limelight".

name: strontium oxide
description: Rock salt's structure again, with heavier strontium; a step down in pitch from CaO.

name: barium oxide
description: Coated on the hot cathodes of vacuum tubes to help them give off electrons.

name: lithium oxide
description: Used in glazes and studied for batteries. Light lithium vibrates fast.

name: calcite
description: Limestone, marble and chalk. Many atoms and three elements make a rich spectrum.
